L1.text: Every morning, Mason found money in his mailbox. One dollar.

L2.text: The next day, two dollars. Then four. Then eight.

L4.text: By day ten, there were over five hundred dollars in there.

L6.text: The officer looked at the money. Then at Mason. And said: someone gives you free money, and you're complaining?

L7.text: He laughed all the way back to his car.

L8.text: By day twenty, the mailbox couldn't even close. Half a million dollars.

L9.text: Mason couldn't sleep. So at three a.m., he hid behind the curtains. And watched.

L10.text: A man in a black mask walked up to the mailbox. And stuffed another bag inside.

L11.text: Then he looked straight at Mason's window. And waved.

L12.text: The next morning, the money was gone. There was only a note.

L13.text: Thanks for keeping it safe. The bank is looking for it everywhere. Except here.

L14.text: That's when the police knocked on the door.

L15.text: Same officer. This time, he wasn't laughing.

L16.text: The masked man? Mason's neighbor. The one who always borrowed his lawnmower. He now lives on a tropical island.

L17.text: And every Christmas, he still sends Mason one dollar.
